prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.

Data extracted. Now the visualization page.Done. Deliverables are in place.

## What I found and built

**The site**: 256 HTML files; 253 are word pages, plus `index.html`, `sobre.html`, `contato.html`, and one redirect stub (`saudades.html` → `saudade.html`). Each word page has an `<h1>` (the canonical word, e.g. `Sofrer.html` → "sofrer"), a `Tema:` line, and relation sections — exactly two relation types exist across the whole site: **Sinônimos** and **Palavras análogas**. Pages cross-link to each other, with 7 dead links (e.g. `rascunho-3.html`, `pagina-removida.html`) which I excluded, since a relation to a page that doesn't exist is not a word in this universe.

**Data** (`./words.json`): 250 words, each mapped to `{tema, links: {relation type → linked words}}`. Relations are treated as undirected (stored on both endpoints, original relation label preserved), links resolved by target file → canonical `<h1>` word, so case-inconsistent filenames (`DOR`, `Nacao`) and URL-encoded names (`fam%C3%ADlia.html`) collapse correctly. `?word=saudade` resolves: tema *sentimentos*, sinônimos *esperança, nostalgia*; análogas *ansiedade, carinho, dor*.

**Result** (`./result.json`): **250 words**, **743 distinct relation pairs**, most connected: **palavra** and **tempo** (16 links each), then advogado, alma, almoço, capital, herança, madrugada, pais, pescador (9 each).

**View** (`./universe/index.html`): a single self-contained file with all data inlined (so it works from `file://` — no fetch, no build). It renders a Three.js (0.170.0 from jsdelivr) 3D force-graph of the whole universe: nodes sized by degree and colored by tema (12 themes), labels always readable, with hand-rolled orbit controls (drag to rotate, wheel to zoom) since the CDN scope excludes OrbitControls addons. Searching filters with autocomplete (arrow keys + Enter); selecting a word dims everything except it and its neighbors, opens a side panel listing its relations grouped by type with clickable chips, and rewrites the URL to `?word=…` — so a shared link like `universe/index.html?word=saudade` opens that word directly (case-insensitive, with a fallback that shows suggestions for unknown words). Google Fonts (Cormorant Garamond / IBM Plex Sans) provides the typography.

**Why I trust it**: the scraper only accepted links resolving to a real word page, and I verified the tricky cases — the `saudades.html` redirect stub is correctly not a word; dead links are counted and excluded (7); `words.json` spot-checks (`acento`, `saudade`) match the raw HTML of those pages; pair count (743) is computed as distinct unordered pairs; the embedded page JS passes a syntax check and the data blob round-trips as valid JSON.

**Assumptions stated**: relations are symmetric (the site lists them one-way but the dictionary reads as an undirected web); only the two existing relation types appear; `<h1>` is the word's identity (filenames/case are not); `sobre`/`contato`/`index` are navigation, not words; links to nonexistent pages are noise and dropped.
